notes:
Summary: mid-market SaaS (B2B product analytics) evaluating Redwood for in-app assistant + similarity search. Started on Hosted API; looking to evaluate Dedicated for predictable throughput and data isolation.

Key constraints: sensitive customer PII in prompts, EU data residency requirements for EU customers, SOC2 reqs, single-sign on required for staff.

Technical targets and POC goals:
- Latency: 95th < 250ms for 512-token chat flows (soft), aiming for <200ms after tuning.
- Throughput: steady-state ~200-400 reqs/sec during business hours, spike up to 1.5x for launches.
- Cost sensitivity: moderate — willing to pay for reserved nodes to ensure consistent latency but need unit economics analysis.
- Model preference: open-ish models first (quantized 4-bit Llama-family variant) on Dedicated; fallback to Redwood-hosted curated model variants for edge cases.
- Quality monitoring: run A/B prompt evals with Redwood Optimize; use prompt-based evals for regression alerts.

POC scope (6 weeks suggested):
- Week 0: contract + infra provisioning (dedicated pool in us-east + us-west), baseline metrics collection on Hosted API
- Week 1-2: deploy model variant A on Dedicated; enable prefix KV caching and batching configs; run synthetic load tests
- Week 3: canary (10% production traffic) routing plan: route 10% live user traffic to Dedicated, 90% to Hosted; compare latency/cost/quality for identical prompts
- Week 4: scale to 40% if canary stable; run failover exercises (region failover us-east -> us-west -> fallback to hosted region)
- Week 5: stress tests and rollback drills; define automatic rollback triggers (error rate >3% or p95 latency >2x SLO sustained for 10m)
- Week 6: handoff and SLO definition; finalize pricing, commit recommendations

Canary + fallback routing details (from SE proposal):
- Canary config: initial 10% traffic, gradually increased to 40% after stable metrics for 48h.
- Fallback routing: if Dedicated reports capacity pressure or elevated latency (>1.5x SLO), route new requests to hosted-api model-variant (lower-cost/compat) or to smaller quantized model variant in another region.
- Model variants: amp-llama-q4 (Dedicated preferred), amp-llama-q4f (fast but lower quality) as fallback, hosted-redwood-v1 for emergency failover.
- Region failover plan: primary pool us-east-1, secondary us-west-2; if both show >30% increase in tail latency, route to hosted API in eu-west-1 (for EU-resident requests use eu pool).
- Rollback: automated rollback to previous stable model/version if 5xx rate >1% sustained for 5m OR quality drift detected by eval probes. Manual rollback action mapped to SE/AE on-call runbook.

Sales/Commercial notes:
- Interested in 12-month reserved commit if POC shows 30% lower cost per inference vs hosted at target latency.
- Legal asked for DPA and KMS integration clause changes — in review.
- Budget holder: VP Product (Maya Ortega) — needs one-pager on unit economics and SLO guarantees.

Quotes and paraphrases: "If Dedicated can guarantee consistent p95 at our 200–250ms target, we'll move to Reserved. Otherwise we stick with hosted and optimize caching" — VP Product.

Next actions (short): finalize SOW, legal reviews DPA, provision dev Dedicated pool, schedule canary start date, technical alignment doc from SE (Liam).
